name: Facet
text: We should implement a dark theme by default with a persistent light-theme toggle. This choice enhances visibility and reduces eye strain, which contributes to user clarity and enjoyment, aligning with our goal of an engaging interface. The trade-off is that some users may prefer a light theme as their default setting, but the dark theme suits the majority of users and current design trends, promoting an overall better experience.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users won’t switch from dark to light even when glare or sunlight demands it, because the toggle becomes noise. A better alternative: default to system preference, with a persistent *high-contrast* toggle instead—visibility stays adaptive, glare is handled, and the toggle serves a real need. Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and glare complaints in both setups.

name: Facet
text:
Default to the system’s theme setting on first load, with a persistent high-contrast toggle that overrides both themes when activated. This keeps glare out of users’ eyes automatically while letting them force visibility when needed, which maximizes both clarity and enjoyment without relying on a theme switch they’ll ignore. The trade-off is a slightly more complex initial setup, but it removes the habituation problem and guarantees the interface adapts to real-world lighting without extra thought.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk is habituation to the high-contrast toggle—users won’t disable it even in low-glare conditions, because it becomes the new default. A better alternative: default to system preference, with a *temporary* high-contrast override (resets after session) and a *persistent* light-theme toggle for permanent glare cases. Settle it with A/B testing: measure glare complaints vs. toggle usage over two weeks.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: We will default to system preference with a temporary high-contrast override that resets after each session and a persistent light-theme toggle, delivering an adaptive interface that balances visibility, clarity, and enjoyment, and the design team owns the implementation of this feature.
